caption:
One ordinary day on Germany's railways: 43,124 scheduled train services, all moving at once.

Watch 7,540 stations light up — ICE, IC and EC long-distance trains threading through a dense mesh of RE, RB and S-Bahn services.

📊 See a full day of German rail traffic in this animated flow map, built from the published DB and DELFI GTFS timetable for Thursday 3 September 2026. Explore how Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt and Munich anchor the busiest network in Europe.

Source: gtfs.de, aggregating Deutsche Bahn and DELFI timetables (CC BY 4.0). Positions are interpolated between the published stops; stations are joined in straight lines, as the GTFS carries no track geometry. Service classes are derived from the line name.
